```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about SpecStory Claude Code CLI installation:

## SpecStory CLI Overview

Claude Code gives you an AI pair-programmer directly in the terminal. Run it through SpecStory to capture every step of the conversation and reasoning as Markdown that ships with your repo.

## Installation Methods

You can install SpecStory using: `brew tap specstoryai/tap && brew install specstory`

Once installed, you can launch Claude Code with auto-save using: `specstory run claude`

## Key Features

SpecStory integrates seamlessly with your favorite AI coding tools, automatically saving all conversations locally to .specstory/history/ in your project. Everything is local-first - your data stays on your machine unless you choose to sync to the cloud.

While the wrapper is active you can use the full Claude Code feature set, including multi-file edits, /init, /clear, and slash commands.

## Additional Commands

Convert prior sessions with specstory sync. This allows you to export existing Claude Code sessions to markdown format.

The SpecStory CLI wrapper works transparently with Claude Code, requiring no additional configuration while preserving all your AI development conversations locally.
```

```text
# SpecStory CLI Installation Commands

## macOS (Homebrew)
The documentation provides these exact commands:
```
brew tap specstoryai/tap
brew update
brew install specstory
specstory version
specstory check
```

## Linux/WSL (Manual Installation)
For Linux systems, the guide states: "Download the archive that matches your OS and architecture (for example `SpecStoryCLI_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz`)" from the [latest release](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/releases).

The exact commands are:
```
tar -xzf SpecStoryCLI_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz
sudo mv specstory /usr/local/bin/
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/specstory
specstory version
```

## Important Notes
- No curl install script is provided in the documentation
- The page emphasizes: "Swap the archive name for the asset you downloaded and repeat when upgrading"
- For macOS upgrades, use `brew upgrade specstory` instead of `brew install`
```

One thing worth noting: SpecStory writes session history into `.specstory/` in the project. You'll probably want to add that to `.gitignore` (or decide to commit it intentionally) before your next commit. Want me to check the current `.gitignore` and add it?
